concept: Atlas disk decrease by volume replacement on AWS, Azure and GCP

claims.text: Atlas documents the same capacity-decrease mechanism for AWS, Azure and Google Cloud: provision new volumes and synchronize data from the old volumes. AWS capacity decreases always use this mechanism regardless of the volume-modification cooldown. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas documents capacity reduction on Google Cloud through replacement volumes and data transfer; this does not mean Compute Engine's disks.resize API supports shrinking, because that API explicitly permits only increases. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Crossplane provider issue #191 records Atlas rejecting a disk decrease below existing data usage with DISK_SIZE_GB_TOO_SMALL. Its example involves reconciliation reapplying an old 40 GB setting after auto-scaling to 80 GB; the issue was closed on October 21, 2026 after an upstream dependency update. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-21)

AWS EBS and Azure data disks cannot be directly downsized; Google Compute Engine's disks.resize API permits only increases. These restrictions explain why an Atlas disk decrease requires replacement storage rather than shrinking the existing cloud disk. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Microsoft's general Azure downsizing guidance explicitly uses a smaller new data disk, data copying, transfer verification, and removal of the old disk. This corroborates the replacement approach, but is VM guidance rather than instructions for operating Atlas-managed disks. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-16)

An AWS IOPS reduction does not inherently require a capacity decrease or data migration: Atlas can lower IOPS in place without restarting nodes after the applicable cooldown; before that it may provision replacement volumes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A first-hand Azure Atlas account originally published in 2021 reports that storage downgrades removed oplog history and invalidated saved change-stream resume positions. Treat this as a historical incident lead, not proof that every current Azure disk decrease has that effect. (low confidence)

For AWS storage-capacity decreases, Atlas documents provisioning replacement volumes and transferring data to them regardless of the volume-modification cooldown; waiting for the cooldown does not enable an in-place EBS capacity decrease. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas documents capacity reduction on Azure through replacement volumes and data transfer, which works around Azure's prohibition on directly downsizing an existing data disk. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Google's native Persistent Disk Terraform guidance warns that specifying a smaller size without an image or snapshot destroys the existing disk and creates an empty replacement; this is not a data-preserving shrink or evidence of Atlas's managed behavior. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26)
